newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Eight killed in Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Eight killed in Karachi violence.

text.p: Eight people, including a policeman, were killed in violent incidents in the Pakistani city of Karachi on Saturday, police said.
There was no immediate word on the motive for any of the separate attacks. Violence has risen in recent weeks amid tension between rival wings of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM).
Police said two gunmen on a motorcycle shot dead police constable Shah Murad, 35, near New Town police station.
In a separate incident, gunmen kidnapped, tortured and hanged a 22-year-old man, before dumping his body in a sewer in the volatile Liaquatabad area of District Central.

A 25-year-old man identified only as Sardar was stabbed to death in District South. Dir Faraz, 30, was shot dead in Quaidabad and gunfire killed Syed Mumtaz Hussain in North Nazimabad in District Central. Three other people were killed in separate areas of the southern port city.

The latest killings brought this week's death toll in Karachi to at least 22. More than 70 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian violence in the city this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
